$comment: The PORT_LIMITATION sites that stay, and why. A site stays only if GATK 4.7.0.0 gives no stable bytes for that run (an unseeded generator, an identity hash, a clock, a host name, memory the reference does not own), or if the run needs a service outside the machine (a Spark cluster, Google Cloud Storage, HDFS, a remote GenomicsDB workspace). Each entry names the file and a phrase of the port's message, which outlive line numbers. Every other site is a feature to port: see the inventory in the body of IPNP-BIPN/gatk-rs#1579.

sites.match: submits the job to a cluster
sites.why: The job is submitted to a Spark master the port has no client for; local masters are run in process.

sites.match: needs a Google Cloud Storage and an HDFS
sites.why: The tool copies a gs:// directory into HDFS, two services outside the machine.

sites.match: The Broad bucket (gs://) is not reachable
sites.arguments: the download from the Broad bucket
sites.why: The data sources live in a gs:// bucket.

sites.match: on a remote file system needs a client
sites.arguments: a gs://, hdfs:// or other remote input or workspace
sites.why: The workspace or the inputs are on a remote file system.

sites.match: is not on a local file system
sites.tools: GenotypeGVCFs, SelectVariants and the other walkers reading gendb://
sites.why: The workspace is on a remote file system.

sites.match: writes what its buffers flushed before the JVM
sites.why: Each task writes through its own buffered stream and the file holds whatever the JVM flushed before it exited.
new Random() is seeded from the clock.
The germline sites are sampled by an unseeded generator.

sites.match: cut by Collections.shuffle without a generator
sites.arguments: --permutect-training-dataset or --permutect-test-dataset with a read set above its downsampling count
sites.why: Collections.shuffle without a Random draws from a clock-seeded one.
The native assembler's assertion ends the JVM, so the reference leaves no output to match.

sites.match: reads memory fermi-lite does not own
sites.arguments: an assembly that reads past fermi-lite's buffers
sites.why: The reference's answer depends on whatever its heap holds there.

sites.match: the reference fails this inside a Spark task
sites.arguments: --attributes-to-clear with a name that is not two characters
sites.why: The task fails while Hadoop writes, which leaves temporary directories named by the job's clock, and with --sanitize the message names the executor's host.

sites.arguments: an MI tag that is a numeric array
sites.why: getAttributeAsString falls through to Object.toString, whose identity hash is the JVM's.
